heading: Meet the Cats
introduction: Explore the projects a computing commons can support. Browsing does not enroll you or start Catnap.

cats.name: The first Catnap
cats.tagline: Watch a deliberately small computation travel through the Commons.
cats.description: The current browser pilot performs a bounded, signed SHA-256 hash-chain task in a JavaScript Web Worker. Its purpose is to demonstrate consent checks, task leasing, verification and receipts—not to claim a scientific breakthrough.
cats.contribution: If an approved Cat matches your personal PoliC, your browser can help complete short hashing tasks after you separately enroll and press Start Catnap.
cats.availability: Requires an approved matching Cat and your explicit consent
cats.review: Featured for explanation; not an approval or trust decision

cats.name: Open climate validation
cats.tagline: A possible future Cat for checking open environmental predictions.
cats.description: Illustrative project: compare archived forecasts with public observations and report reproducible error metrics. No such general workload is offered by this browser pilot.
cats.contribution: A future Catbox might process publicly licensed datasets in bounded batches, with terms and resource limits reviewed before any execution.
cats.availability: Concept only — not available for Catnap
cats.review: Illustrative idea; not submitted or approved

cats.name: Cultural archive research
cats.tagline: A possible future Cat for permissioned digital preservation.
cats.description: Illustrative project: help researchers organize openly licensed or permissioned cultural material with auditable provenance and rights-aware participation.
cats.contribution: Future contributors could opt into narrowly specified tasks only after a Cat has a public repository, signed constitution, reviewed Catbox and compatible worker runtime.
cats.availability: Concept only — not available for Catnap
cats.review: Illustrative idea; not submitted or approved
